But while it was all in a day's work to Eamonn, poor Mick Nouch, in his first ever 5000m at this level, found himself completely run out after 11½ laps and reeled off the track in a bad way with the bell ringing in his ears.

It was great also to welcome into the team long time members who have only recently turned 40, Reg Hopkins and Mike Nouch. Reg got such a 'buzz' from racing again that he was reputed to be training daily during the next few weeks.

Jim Estall was in a different class to the rest, going away all the time, and with Mick Nouch running his heart out to pass a black-vested rival in the straight and Laurie O'Hara doing likewise and setting M55 and M60 records in the process, the tide was gradually turning.

First Belgravian home was Mike Nouch in 9th, running slightly slower than his best time in 26:50. Laurie, now 63, finished 17th in the race in 28:38 and was only 40 seconds outside his record time.
